name: Palace Hotel (original)
shape_note: 755 rooms; 120 ft (37 m), 7 storeys of balconies round a skylit Grand Court (carriage entrance). Tallest building in SF 1875-1890. Burned 1906; new Palace opened 1909 on the same site. Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM relation/3492933.

name: Chronicle (de Young) Building
shape_note: SF's first skyscraper (Burnham & Root): 218 ft (66 m) incl. 4-storey clock tower, 10 storeys. Clock tower burned 7 Nov 1905; two floors added + 16-storey Kearny annex begun 1905-06; gutted 1906, rebuilt by Polk 1908; re-clad 1962 (now Ritz-Carlton Club). Model the 1890 form 1890-1905. Location: coord from source.

name: Call (Claus Spreckels) Building
shape_note: 315 ft (96 m), 15 storeys incl. domed cupola; tallest in the West. Gutted 1906, restored; 1938 remodel removed the dome and raised it to 21 floors at 299 ft (now Central Tower). Model the domed form 1898-1938. Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/132127810.

name: Hearst (Examiner) Building
shape_note: Six storeys, SE corner Market/Third (Newspaper Row). Demolished after 1906; replaced by the present 12-storey Hearst Building (1909). Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/132127809.

name: Mills Building
shape_note: 10 storeys, 154 ft (47 m) (Burnham & Root). Survived the quake, burned out 1906, restored by Polk 1907; 22-storey tower added 1931-32 (separate). Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM relation/3492808.

name: Crocker Building
shape_note: 11-storey flatiron at Market/Post/Montgomery (A. Page Brown). Damaged 1906, rebuilt; demolished 1968 for the Montgomery BART/Muni station plaza. Height not found (11 storeys ~ 45-50 m, ESTIMATE). Location: geocoded S corner of Post St & Market St (DataSF centerlines, +-30 m).

name: Phelan Building (first)
shape_note: Six-storey flatiron on the triangle Market/O'Farrell/Grant; dynamited 20 Apr 1906; new Phelan Building 1907-08 on the same lot. Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM relation/1547962.

name: Baldwin Hotel and Theatre
shape_note: Theatre completed 1875, hotel built around it 1876 (Sumner Bugbee); destroyed by fire 1898; Flood Building (1904) built on the site. Storey count not in sources (photos suggest ~6 incl. mansard: ESTIMATE). Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: coord from source.

name: James Flood Building
shape_note: 12 storeys (Albert Pissis), on the Baldwin Hotel site; gutted 1906 and restored; standing. Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM relation/1547963.

name: Grand Opera House (Wade's Opera House)
shape_note: Mission St between 3rd and 4th (north side); 2,395 seats, stage 42 x 74 ft. Built 1874 per nesssoftware, opened 17 Jan 1876 per Wikipedia. Caruso sang Carmen here 17 Apr 1906; destroyed 18 Apr 1906. Location: coord from source.

name: California Theatre
shape_note: 414 (now 440) Bush St; built 1869 by William Ralston (S. C. Bugbee & Son); rebuilt May 1889 on the same site; destroyed 1906. Location: coord from source.

name: Occidental Hotel
shape_note: Montgomery St between Bush and Sutter; opened 1861, closed 18 Apr 1906 (burned). Location: coord from source.

name: Montgomery Block ("Monkey Block")
shape_note: 628 Montgomery, SE corner Washington; ~50 ft (15 m), 4 storeys, U-shaped around a light court; SF's first fireproof building, survived 1906; demolished 1959 (Transamerica Pyramid site). Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/24222973.

name: Parrott Building (Granite Block)
shape_note: NW corner California/Montgomery, built 1852 of granite cut in China; survived 1906; demolished 1926 (Omni Hotel/Financial Center Building site). Storeys not given (photos: 3, ESTIMATE). Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/1279459281.

name: Merchants Exchange (second)
shape_note: Three-storey building with a tower, south side of California at Montgomery; replaced on the same site by the 12-storey Merchants Exchange (1904). End year = start of replacement (ESTIMATE). Location: coord from source.

name: Merchants Exchange Building
shape_note: 12-storey skyscraper by Burnham & Polk (465 California); heavily damaged 1906, rebuilt by Polk and Julia Morgan; standing (Wikipedia gives 15 floors today). Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: coord from source.

name: Mutual Savings Bank Building
shape_note: 12 storeys (Curlett & Moore), five-sided lot between Market and Geary (700 Market); interior burned 1906; standing. Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: coord from source.

name: Hayward (Kohl) Building
shape_note: NE corner California/Montgomery (Percy & Polk); one of the first steel-frame "fireproof" buildings in California; minor 1906 damage; standing (OSM: 9 levels). Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/690663633.

name: St. Francis Hotel (south wings)
shape_note: Two 12-storey south wings opened 21 Mar 1904 (NW corner Powell/Geary); fire-damaged 1906, reopened 1907; third wing 1908, fourth 1913 (full Powell frontage); tower 1971. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/332378158.

name: Emporium (Parrott Building #2)
shape_note: 835 Market between 4th and 5th (Albert Pissis). Date conflict: nesssoftware says commissioned early 1890s / 1898; the store opened 1896 (ESTIMATE). Gutted 1906, rebuilt behind the facade; now Westfield San Francisco Centre. Location: geocoded mid-block Market St between 4th St and 5th St (+-40 m).

name: Hibernia Bank
shape_note: 1 Jones St (Jones/McAllister/Market); survived 1906 with damage; addition 1908; standing. Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/35536650.

name: U.S. Mint ("Old Mint")
shape_note: Built 1869-74 at 5th/Mission; survived the 1906 fire (staff fought it); mint moved 1937; standing. Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/32863779.

name: Appraiser's Building (first)
shape_note: Sansome St east side between Washington and Jackson, built 1877; survived 1906 (fire fought from the roof). Replaced on the same block by the present Appraisers Building (completed 1944); end year ESTIMATE (demolition date not found). Location: geocoded mid-block Sansome St between Washington St and Jackson St (+-40 m).

name: Old St. Mary's (St. Mary's Cathedral 1854-91)
shape_note: California & Grant NE corner, built 1853-54; tower 90 ft (27 m) - tallest building in SF 1854-75; gutted 1906, restored inside the walls by 1909; standing. Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/260520154.

name: St. Mary's Cathedral (second)
shape_note: NW corner Van Ness/O'Farrell, built 1887-91; survived 1906 (west of the firebreak); destroyed by arson 8 Sep 1962. Location: geocoded NW corner of Van Ness Ave & OFarrell St (DataSF centerlines, +-30 m).

name: Grace Church
shape_note: SE corner California/Stockton, built 1862-68 (bell tower added later); destroyed 1906; parish moved to the Crocker mansion block (Grace Cathedral). Location: geocoded SE corner of California St & Stockton St (DataSF centerlines, +-30 m).

name: St. Ignatius Church and College
shape_note: Third St. Ignatius Church + College, dedicated 1880 at Van Ness/Hayes (now Davies Symphony Hall site); destroyed 1906; successor church 1910-14 on the USF campus. Footprint: occupied a large part of the block (not measured). Location: geocoded NW corner of Van Ness Ave & Hayes St (DataSF centerlines, +-30 m).

name: Temple Emanu-El (Sutter St)
shape_note: 450 Sutter (north side, between Stockton and Powell). Built 1864 (nesssoftware) or 1866 (Wikipedia caption "1866-1926"); gutted 1906, repaired and reopened 1907; congregation moved to Lake St 1926; site now 450 Sutter (1929). Location: geocoded mid-block Sutter St between Stockton St and Powell St (+-40 m).

name: St. Dominic's Church (1887)
shape_note: Steiner/Bush, built 1883-87; heavily damaged 1906 (outside the fire); replaced by the present church built 1923-28 (end year = start of replacement, ESTIMATE). Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/32964914.

name: Mission High School (1898 building)
shape_note: 18th St between Church and Dolores; survived 1906 (refugee centre); destroyed by fire 1922; replaced 1925-27 on the same site. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/24524033.

name: Central Park (baseball grounds)
shape_note: Market/8th to Mission, across Market from City Hall; ~15,000 seats; home of the SF Seals 1903-06; wooden stands burned 1906. Location: geocoded mid-block Market St between 8th St and 8th St (+-40 m).

name: Panorama Building / Tivoli Opera House
shape_note: SW corner Eddy/Mason: Panorama Building (1884), Tivoli Opera House from 1903; destroyed 1906. (Earlier Tivoli 1879 was a house on Eddy near Market.) Location: geocoded SW corner of Eddy St & Mason St (DataSF centerlines, +-30 m).

name: Jenny Lind Theatre / City Hall / Hall of Justice
shape_note: SE corner Kearny/Washington opposite Portsmouth Square: built 1851 as the Jenny Lind Theatre, bought 1852 as City Hall, later the Hall of Justice (1900-06). Whether the 1900 Hall of Justice reused or replaced the 1851 building is unclear in the sources (LOW confidence). Location: geocoded SE corner of Kearny St & Washington St (DataSF centerlines, +-30 m).

name: Mark Hopkins Mansion / Mark Hopkins Institute of Art
material: wood frame, Gothic/Victorian with tall tower
shape_note: SE corner California/Mason; begun 1875 (completion year ESTIMATE 1878); its tower was then the highest point in SF; Mark Hopkins Institute of Art from 1893; burned 1906; Mark Hopkins Hotel 1926 on the site. Granite retaining walls survive. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/1361492525.

name: Leland Stanford Mansion
shape_note: California/Powell (Stanford Court Hotel site); destroyed 1906 except its granite walls (Wikipedia Nob Hill). Start year ESTIMATE (c. 1876, not verified). Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM relation/6480430.

name: Charles Crocker Mansion
shape_note: Block California/Jones/Sacramento/Taylor (now Grace Cathedral); destroyed 1906 (granite walls survive). Start year ESTIMATE (not verified). Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/32946942.

name: Colton / Huntington Mansion
shape_note: Block Sacramento/Taylor/California/Cushman (now Huntington Park, donated 1915); destroyed 1906. Start year ESTIMATE (David Colton house c. 1872, later bought by Huntington; not verified). Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/32946958.

name: James C. Flood Mansion (Pacific-Union Club)
shape_note: 1000 California St, built 1886; first brownstone west of the Mississippi; gutted 1906, rebuilt by Willis Polk as the Pacific-Union Club (wings added). Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the present building on the same lot (Overture), a proxy for the lot. Location: centroid of successor/same building OSM way/32947069.

name: Bonet Electric Tower (Midwinter Fair)
shape_note: 266 ft (81 m) Eiffel-style steel tower with 3,200 lights at the centre of the Grand Court of Honor (today's Music Concourse), Midwinter Fair 27 Jan-4 Jul 1894; stood ~2 years, then demolished with explosives at McLaren's request (end year ESTIMATE 1896). Location: coord from source.

name: Midwinter Fair Fine Arts Building (first de Young Museum)
shape_note: Built for the 1894 fair; became the first de Young Museum. End year ESTIMATE (demolished c. 1929 after the 1919-25 de Young wings; not verified). Location ESTIMATE: north side of the Music Concourse (de Young site). Location: coord from source.
